body_markdown:
*Industry publication also recognizes FreeCast as its Home Streaming Solution Company of the Year, highlighting its unified media platform, enterprise PaaS technology and expanding monetization opportunities.*


FreeCast, Inc. (NASDAQ: CAST), a media technology company providing a software-based Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) for streaming, television distribution and monetization, today announced its recognition by Media & Entertainment Business Review as its Streaming Technology Platform Company of the Year 2026.


The publication also identifies FreeCast as its Home Streaming Solution Company of the Year 2026, featuring the company as the sole solution provider on its dedicated Top Home Streaming Solution Companies 2026 page.


The recognition accompanies an extensive company profile in the publication's October–November 2026 edition, highlighting FreeCast's approach to consolidating fragmented television, streaming subscriptions, local broadcasting and digital entertainment through a common software infrastructure.


## **Not Another Streaming Service — A Platform for the Entire Media Industry**


FreeCast's business model differs from traditional streaming services that compete primarily through exclusive programming, subscriber acquisition and content production.


Instead, FreeCast provides technology designed to connect consumers, content providers, broadcasters, telecommunications companies, internet service providers, satellite operators and other enterprises through a shared media platform.


Its software-based infrastructure enables enterprise partners to offer branded entertainment experiences while maintaining their existing customer relationships and participating in potential revenue opportunities from subscriptions, advertising, transactions and digital commerce.


William Mobley, Founder and CEO of FreeCast, commented:


"We believe the television industry is undergoing one of the most important structural transformations in its history. Consumers have more content choices than ever, but the experience has become increasingly fragmented. Meanwhile, companies that already serve millions of customers have an opportunity to provide entertainment and participate in the economics surrounding that engagement."


"FreeCast was built to address both sides of that equation. We're not trying to become another Netflix or compete with the industry's content owners. We're providing the software infrastructure that can help connect the entire media ecosystem."


"Being recognized for our streaming technology platform is particularly meaningful because it reflects the broader role we believe FreeCast can serve, not simply as a consumer entertainment destination, but as an enabling technology for the media industry's next generation of distribution and monetization."


## **One Software Platform, Multiple Revenue Opportunities**


The publication's coverage highlights several components of FreeCast's platform, including:


- SmartGuide: Unified content discovery, recommendations and search across supported free and paid entertainment services.
- YouBundle: Tools designed to simplify subscription selection and management.
- MediaPay: Payment and subscription management capabilities.
- Enterprise PaaS: White-label media technology enabling organizations to offer branded streaming experiences without independently developing the full underlying infrastructure.
- Advertising and Commerce: Monetization capabilities designed to support advertising, subscriptions, transactions and other commercial activity.


FreeCast's enterprise strategy focuses on organizations that already maintain established customer relationships. Rather than relying exclusively on traditional direct-to-consumer subscriber acquisition, the company seeks to expand distribution through business partners serving residential, mobile, commercial and institutional audiences.


The company refers to the potential customers accessible through participating enterprise relationships as Partner-Enabled Addressable Customers (PEAC). This measure represents a potential distribution opportunity, not activated subscribers or recognized revenue.


FreeCast believes this partner-enabled model may provide opportunities to scale its software platform across multiple industries and geographic markets as enterprise deployments progress.


## **Recognition Highlights the Changing Economics of Television**


In its feature titled The Spotify Model Comes to Television, Media & Entertainment Business Review examines FreeCast's approach to bringing together media discovery, subscription management, enterprise distribution and monetization.


The publication also released a companion industry analysis, A Single Front Door for Streaming, examining how unified streaming platforms can address the growing complexity of entertainment discovery and subscription management.


The coverage reflects FreeCast's strategy of positioning its software platform as a common technology layer serving consumers, content owners and distribution partners.


"Connectivity is only the beginning of the customer relationship," Mobley added. "What happens after the connection, how consumers discover entertainment, manage subscriptions, interact with advertising and participate in commerce, represents an opportunity for businesses that already have established audiences."


"We believe the next chapter of television will be defined not simply by who owns the content or delivers the internet connection, but by who can simplify the consumer experience and enable the industry to participate more efficiently in the economic activity around it. That's the opportunity FreeCast is pursuing."

## **About FreeCast, Inc.**


FreeCast, Inc. (NASDAQ: CAST) is a media technology company providing a software-based Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) designed to simplify entertainment discovery, distribution and monetization. FreeCast brings together free and premium streaming, live television, local programming, subscription management, advertising and commerce through a unified platform.


Through its business-to-business-to-consumer (B2B2C) model, FreeCast enables telecommunications providers, internet service providers, satellite operators, broadcasters, property operators, membership organizations and other enterprises to offer branded media experiences while maintaining direct customer relationships.


For more information, visit https://www.freecast.com.
